# Bevy 0.18 module parity — entity-level mismatch tracker

**Reference:** Bevy tag `v0.18.0`, commit `5f8270f2e049f90139a503d1e930070d926f9427`, checked out at `tmp/bevy-0.18.0`.

**Audited modules:** `epix_engine/mesh`, `epix_engine/image`, `epix_engine/sprite`,
`epix_engine/sprite_render`, `epix_engine/pbr`, `epix_engine/render/core_graph`.

**Bevy counterparts:** `bevy_mesh`, `bevy_image`, `bevy_sprite`, `bevy_sprite_render`,
`bevy_pbr` + `bevy_light` (lights, shadows, clusters, fog, light probes and
environment maps were split out of `bevy_pbr` in 0.18), `bevy_core_pipeline`.

## Status of this tracker

This is the authoritative tracker for those six modules. It replaces the earlier
per-module trackers (`mesh-core-graph-bevy-0.18-match-status.md`,
`mesh-primitive-builders-bevy-0.18-mismatch-tracker.md`,
`image-bevy-0.18-mismatch-tracker.md`,
`sprite-bevy-0.18-mismatch-tracker.md`,
`pbr-bevy-0.18-mismatch-tracker.md`), which had drifted in both directions —
rows marked open that were already implemented, and rows marked aligned that
were not — because they recorded conclusions without the entity-level evidence
needed to re-check them. Those files are kept as history only; every claim in
them must be re-derived here against the current sources.

## What a row is

One row per **Bevy entity**, in Bevy's own declaration order inside each Bevy
source file, so each table reads as Bevy's file diffed against Epix:

| Kind | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `type` | a struct / enum / class / type alias |
| `field` | one field of such a type |
| `const` | an associated or module-level constant |
| `method` | a method or member function, signature level |
| `fn` | a free function, signature level |
| `def` | a function/method **body** (implementation logic) |
| `impl` | a trait impl or a coherent group of impls |
| `shader` | one WGSL entry point or shader struct |

A `def` row exists whenever the body's logic is what needs checking — a
declaration can match Bevy exactly while the body diverges. Where a body is
trivially the same shape as its Bevy original, the `method` row carries the
verdict and no `def` row is added.

Rows are kept even when they match: the ✅ rows are the coverage evidence, and
they are what makes an "aligned" claim re-checkable later. Mismatches are simply
the non-✅ rows.

## Columns

`| ID | Kind | Entity | Bevy (file:line) | Epix (file:line) | Status | Difference / required alignment |`

Path convention: the Bevy column is crate-relative (`bevy_mesh/src/mesh.rs:812`),
the Epix column is repository-relative (`epix_engine/mesh/src/mesh.cpp:412`).
Line ranges are used when a range was read. Rows are grouped under
`### <crate>/<path>` headings in Bevy's declaration order.

ID blocks are allocated per Bevy file so that parallel audits cannot collide;
numbering is therefore contiguous inside a block, not across the whole module.
When a block is exhausted the next free block of that module continues it.

## Status legend

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| ✅ | Entity matches Bevy in interface, behaviour, scheduling and logic |
| ❌ | Present but diverges from Bevy — non-intentional, must be aligned |
| ⚠️ | Intentional divergence, with its rationale recorded in the row |
| 🚫 | Missing from Epix — real gap |
| ⛔ | Out of scope for Epix (no counterpart facility, or a Bevy subsystem Epix deliberately does not have) |
| REVIEW | Not yet decided; the row states exactly what could not be determined |

## ID scheme

IDs are module-prefixed and sequential within the module, and are assigned from
Bevy's declaration order so a row can be found by searching the Bevy symbol:

| Prefix | Module |
| --- | --- |
| `MSH-<n>` | `mesh` |
| `IMG-<n>` | `image` |
| `SPR-<n>` | `sprite` |
| `SRD-<n>` | `sprite_render` |
| `PBR-<n>` | `pbr` |
| `CGR-<n>` | `render/core_graph` |
| `PRT-<n>` | a parent module (`render`, `app`, `ecs`, `assets`, `camera`, `transform`, …) that diverges from Bevy and is exposed by this audit |

An ID is stable once assigned: it is never reused or renumbered, and rows are
never deleted. A row whose mismatch is fixed keeps its ID and moves to ✅ with
the fixing commit recorded. This is what allows a commit message, an approval
request and a later re-audit to refer to the same mismatch.

## What counts as a mismatch

Bevy's own source settles design questions — type layout, ownership, naming,
defaults, ordering, bit positions, algorithms, scheduling, error types — and
Epix takes Bevy's shape. Only these are legitimate divergences:

1. **C++-forced.** No traits with associated-type defaults, no specialization,
   no reflection, no field-vs-method overloading, no generic-over-trait APIs,
   no trait objects where Bevy type-erases. A C++-forced divergence still has to
   be verified against the code, not assumed from the shape.
2. **No counterpart facility.** Bevy relies on a subsystem Epix does not have at
   all; the row then records what the missing facility is and what it blocks.
3. **User-accepted.** Explicitly accepted by the user and recorded as ⚠️ or ⛔.

Everything else is ❌ or 🚫 and gets fixed.

Representation is not behaviour: a difference in type shape with identical
observable behaviour is recorded as a shape divergence rather than inflated into
a behaviour mismatch — but it is still recorded, because it is a divergence from
Bevy's shape.

## Verification policy

A row may only be moved to ✅ with the evidence recorded in the row:

- **Logic-only / value-only changes** — the focused module tests, plus the tests
  of every module that consumes the changed type.
- **Any change that can affect rendering** — a whole-tree build, the full CTest
  sweep, and the example sweep on both output streams (`tmp/sweep_examples.ps1`;
  Epix examples log through spdlog, which writes *all* categories including
  error/fatal to **stdout**, so a stderr-only check proves nothing), plus stable
  client-area captures of the rendering examples, inspected as images rather
  than by pixel statistics alone.
- Build and test are never chained in one command; the verified toolchain is the
  MSVC Insider 14.52 toolset on the `msvc-reldeb-no-modules` preset at `-j8`
  (`tmp/build-target.bat`).

**Tests do not shape production code.** Testability is never a reason to
decompose a Bevy-shaped method into smaller pieces or to adapt a data structure
for easier assertions; tests drive the real entry points afterwards.

## Commits

Any fix that requires a change outside the six audited modules — in a parent
module such as `render`, `app`, `ecs`, `assets`, `camera` or `transform` — is
presented to the user for approval before committing, with the mismatch IDs, a
concise description, the changed files and the verification evidence. A parent
module that turns out to diverge is itself a `PARENT:` row: the parent module is
audited again rather than patched around.

One wording note on the Open mismatch index below: its **Epix file that must change** column is filled with the first repository path in the row's Epix cell, else the first repository path in the row's difference cell, and repeats the section's own `none`/`—` only when neither cell names one — 13 of the 571 rows take their path from the difference cell that way, so the column's own note reads more narrowly than the column is actually filled. Earlier disagreements are all corrected in the source sections: `mesh-lead-verified.md` read ✅ 9 for a set that computes to ✅ 11, and its narrative is what resolves the `MSH-1012`/`MSH-1013` pair — the two private helpers are audited in both mesh sections under two ID blocks, and `mesh-mesh_rs.md` (`MSH-151`, `MSH-155`) carries the verdict, which is why those two rows point there rather than re-deriving it; `pbr-lights.md`'s narrative read "The 20 ❌ rows are the actionable findings" and "which is why 239 rows are ✅" against a computed ✅ 243 · ❌ 16, and its numbered list then carried entries for `PBR-576`, `PBR-611`, `PBR-682`, `PBR-798` and `PBR-840` as open after those rows had moved to ✅ (that list has since been rewritten, except for entries 23 and 24 noted above); `core_graph-core3d-core2d.md`'s per-status table was corrected to ✅ 187 · ❌ 6 · ⚠️ 4 · 🚫 9 · ⛔ 3 · REVIEW 2; `image-image_rs.md`'s non-✅ list header read "(92)" where its rows compute 87; and the "Next candidates" list that still held the six `image.rs` ❌ rows as open after batch 9 was replaced by the batch 1-17 list. The rule stands: rows win, and any future disagreement is recorded here rather than silently patched. Three section files are stored with CRLF line endings (`image-loader-atlas.md`, `pbr-render-mesh.md`, `pbr-lights.md`); all are merged here with the repository's LF convention, content unchanged. Every summary in the Open mismatch index is its row's own `Difference / required alignment` text cut to its first clause(s) — all 571 were re-checked against the merged sections and each is a prefix of that text — and every **ID** and **Status** cell is copied from its row unchanged.

Every non-✅ row from every merged section, grouped by module and, inside a module, in section and Bevy declaration order. The ⚠️ and ⛔ rows are listed on purpose: they are the record of intentional and out-of-scope divergences, not open work. **ID** and **Status** are copied from the section row unchanged; the **one-line summary** is the row's own `Difference / required alignment` text cut to its first clause(s); **Epix file that must change** is the first repository path in the row's Epix cell, or — when that cell names no path — the first path named in the row's difference cell. Where the Epix cell says `none` or `—`, the section records no Epix file at all (the entity is missing rather than misplaced), so the cell repeats the section's own value instead of inventing a target.

## Fix batches

A batch is a set of rows fixed together, verified together, and (when it touches
a parent module) approved together. A row moves to ✅ only when its batch is
verified; the fixing commit is recorded here.

### Batch 1 — `Mesh` owns its packed vertex data (MSH-1002 … MSH-1007)

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Mismatch IDs | `MSH-1002`, `MSH-1003`, `MSH-1004`, `MSH-1005`, `MSH-1006`, `MSH-1007` (and the deletion of the Epix-only `render::mesh::vertex_array_stride` / `packed_vertex_bytes` recorded in those rows) |
| Bevy behaviour | `Mesh` owns the vertex-size and packed-vertex-data API: `get_vertex_size` (`bevy_mesh/src/mesh.rs:822`), `get_vertex_buffer_size` (`:835`), `create_packed_vertex_buffer_data` (`:932`), `write_packed_vertex_buffer_data` (`:947`); `bevy_render`'s allocator consumes them (`bevy_render/src/mesh/allocator.rs:479,538-546`). |
| Epix divergence | The four methods did not exist; the same arithmetic lived in the *parent* `render` module as the free functions `vertex_array_stride` / `packed_vertex_bytes`, and the allocator called those. |
| Change | Added the four methods to `epix::mesh::Mesh` with Bevy's definitions, deleted the two render-side helpers, and switched `MeshAllocator::allocate_meshes` to `get_vertex_buffer_size()` / `create_packed_vertex_buffer_data()`. |
| Files | `epix_engine/mesh/include/epix/mesh/mesh.hpp`, `epix_engine/mesh/src/mesh.cpp`, `epix_engine/mesh/tests/header/module_test.cpp`, `epix_engine/mesh/tests/module/module_test.cpp`, `epix_engine/render/render/include/epix/render/mesh/render_asset.hpp`, `epix_engine/render/render/src/mesh.cpp`, `epix_engine/render/render/src/mesh_allocator.cpp`, `epix_engine/render/render/tests/header/mesh_allocator_tests.cpp` |
| Tests | New `MeshModule.VertexPackingMatchesBevy` (empty mesh, size/buffer size, interleaved byte order, write-form equals create-form, truncation to the smallest attribute count); the two render tests that called the deleted helpers now drive `Mesh::get_vertex_size` / `create_packed_vertex_buffer_data`. |
| Verification | Whole-tree build `BUILD_EXIT=0` (`tmp/audit-build-mesh-packing.log`); CTest `92/92 passed`; `tests_header_mesh_module_test.exe` 89 tests green; `tests_header_render_mesh_allocator_tests.exe` 27 tests green; example sweep over 62 examples on both streams (`tmp/audit-sweep-mesh-packing/`) with one flagged example — `fallingsand_falling_sand`, the *same* `specialize material2d meshes` error already present in `tmp/sweep/` (2026-09-21), `tmp/sweep-spirv-final/` and `tmp/sweep-s11-final/` (2026-09-19), i.e. pre-existing and not caused by this batch; stable client-area captures of `examples_header_mesh_rendering` and `examples_header_mesh_batching` (3 identical-hash frames each, 0 stderr bytes, `tmp/audit-capture-mesh-packing/`, `tmp/audit-capture-mesh-batching/`), inspected visually: all meshes render with correct positions, UVs, colours and blending. |
| Parent modules touched | `render` — approved by the user before committing, as the policy's *Commits* section requires. |
| Status | **committed as `f134b53f`** — `refactor(mesh): own the vertex packing API (MSH-1002..MSH-1007)` |

### Batch 2 — `Sprite`'s requirements and visibility class (SPR-117, SPR-120, SPR-128, SPR-129)

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Mismatch IDs | `SPR-117`, `SPR-120` (AABB insert mode), `SPR-128` (`#[require(...)]` registered from the plugin), `SPR-129` (visibility class not appended) |
| Bevy behaviour | Both declarations are intrinsic to the component: `#[require(Transform, Visibility, VisibilityClass, Anchor)]` (`bevy_sprite/src/sprite.rs:15`) and `#[component(on_add = visibility::add_visibility_class::<Sprite>)]` (`:17`); `calculate_bounds_2d` inserts with `try_insert` (`bevy_sprite/src/lib.rs:153,190`). |
| Epix divergence | The four requirements were registered from `SpritePlugin::attach`, and the visibility class as a required-component *constructor*, which only runs when the component is absent — so a `Mesh2d`-then-`Sprite` entity never gained the `Sprite` class and `queue_sprites_2d` skipped it. The two new-bounds branches used `insert_if_new`, so on a dual `Mesh2d`+`Sprite` entity the mesh bounds survived instead of the sprite bounds, and neither update query could refresh them because both carry the `Without<...>` disjointness filters. |
| Change | `Sprite::register_required_components` and `Sprite::on_add` carry Bevy's two declarations; `SpritePlugin::attach` only registers the component. Both `calculate_bounds_2d` branches insert with `EntityCommands::insert`. |
| Files | `epix_engine/sprite/include/epix/sprite/sprite.hpp`, `epix_engine/sprite/src/sprite.cpp`, `epix_engine/sprite/tests/header/sprite_parity_tests.cpp` |

### Batch 45 — the runtime-sized minimum binding size in the render contract (PRT-5, parent `render`)

For a runtime-sized array it is the element's shader size, and for a struct containing one it is the fixed prefix plus one element, rounded up to the struct's alignment (`encase-0.12.1/src/types/runtime_sized_array.rs:130-144`, `encase_derive_impl-0.12.1/src/lib.rs:676-680`); the trait's own doc says so ("this will be calculated by assuming the array has one element", `encase-0.12.1/src/core/traits.rs:88-96`). |

The render parity probe encoded the same rule, asserting `shader_size == sizeof(std::uint32_t)` for a header-plus-array type. Batch 44 had already corrected the three pbr specialisations that followed it. |
| Change | Both doc blocks reworded to the one-element rule, and the parity probe's `ShaderTypeInfo` now reports `2 * sizeof(std::uint32_t)` — the header plus one element — with the assertion message and comments saying why. No production behaviour changes: `StorageBuffer::write_buffer` uses `size_for`, not `shader_size`. |

### Batch 55 — the occlusion-culling, morph and skinning shader helpers (PBR-307..PBR-309)

| Field | Value |

| Bevy behaviour | `occlusion_culling.wgsl` has the two depth-pyramid helpers that size an AABB in pixels and read the occluder depth from the four texels the AABB covers (`render/occlusion_culling.wgsl:5-30`). `morph.wgsl` declares the morph weights and the target texture as the mesh layout's group-2 bindings 2, 3 and 7, and reads a vertex's morph component back out of the texture with Bevy's hardcoded offsets (`render/morph.wgsl:3-52`). `skinning.wgsl` declares the joint matrices as a uniform block or a storage buffer per `SKINS_USE_UNIFORM_BUFFERS`, plus the previous frame's at binding 6, and has the weighted-sum transform, its previous-frame twin, the 3x3 inverse transpose and the normal transform (`render/skinning.wgsl:3-95`). |
| Epix divergence | None of the three existed; `mesh.wgsl` and the vertex stage's helpers had no counterpart. |
| Change | All three join `pbr/src/mesh_shaders.cpp` and the embedded set, each at Bevy's group-2 bindings and def gates. The one representation rule they needed is stated at the top of the skinning module: Slang matrices are row-major where WGSL's are column-major, so the port keeps Bevy's matrices transposed — `M[i]` reads the same column, a `mat3x3(c0, c1, c2)` is a `float3x3` whose rows are those columns, and `M * v` becomes `mul(v, M)`. With that rule the two matrix functions are Bevy's bodies unchanged, and the scalar-times-matrix accumulation is orientation-free either way. |

### Batch 81 — the binding-array mechanism is pinned down by disproof, not by guess

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Mismatch IDs | none closed; `PBR-319` gains the concrete finding below, and `PBR-269`'s bindless branch stays open |
| Epix divergence | Unchanged — the bindless lightmap branch is absent. |
| Change | **No code change**: the attempt was reverted in full, and the reason is the valuable part. The entry shape Bevy uses (`entry::lightmaps_texture_view_array(4, &texture_views)`) has no direct C counterpart, and the obvious hypothesis for wgpu-native — one entry per array element, with the first carrying the length in a chained `wgpu::BindGroupEntryExtras` and the rest following as further entries — is **wrong**. A device test proved it: `Number of bindings in bind group descriptor (9) does not match the number of bindings defined in the bind group layout (3)` for a 4-slot slab. wgpu-native counts the descriptor's entries against the layout before any extras are consulted, so the array's elements cannot be carried as extra entries. |
| Also established | `WGPUBindGroupEntryExtras` is **not** in the `webgpu.h` the build uses (`_deps/wgpu-windows-x86_64-msvc-release-src/include/webgpu/webgpu.h`), although the wrapper declares it and exposes `setBufferCount`/`setSamplerCount`/`setTextureViewCount`. So the count setters alone are evidently not the whole story, and the next attempt should start from the wrapper's own source (`libs/webgpu-wrapper`) and the wgpu-native release headers it wraps, rather than from the generated wrapper. |
| Files | none (reverted; tree re-verified at `51ba7e45`) |
| Tests | The device test that disproved the hypothesis is itself reverted; `MeshBindGroups.EveryVariantIsCreatedFromItsLayout` is green again at the batch-80 state, covering every non-bindless variant. |
| Verification | Build `BUILD=0`; the bind-group test rebuilt and passing; the rest of the suite unaffected (no other file touched). |
| Parent modules touched | none |
| Status | none — a record, not a commit of code |
| Note | This is the second time a plausible mechanism for the binding-array entries has failed on contact (the first was a plain slice, batch 80). The lesson is worth writing down rather than repeating: for this one API the generated wrapper is not a sufficient specification — the answer is in the wrapper's own implementation, and until it is read there, every attempt is a guess that a device test must be trusted to reject. |

### Batch 84 — the port's own constrained templates were malformed and under-constrained

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Mismatch IDs | none — these are defects of the port's own helper templates, found in review, not divergences from Bevy |
| What was wrong (1) | `EPIX_EXPORT` is the C++20 `export` keyword, and `export` may only appear **before** a template-head. Four sites read `template <..> requires .. EPIX_EXPORT ret f(..)`, which is ill-formed; they compile today only because the module build is not the one being built (the macro expands to nothing in the non-module build), which is exactly how a silent break hides. Fixed to `EPIX_EXPORT template <..> requires ...`. |
| What was wrong (2) | Every one of the four constraints stopped at invocability and never constrained the **result**, which is what carries the contract. Three callables are used as predicates — `if (!in_view(object_sphere))`, `if (!in_view(object.sphere()))`, `if (!mapper(clusterable, render_entity))` — so their result must be convertible to `bool`; `cached_cluster_sphere`'s result is assigned to a `std::optional<camera::Sphere>`, so it must yield a `camera::Sphere`. Bevy's own bounds name the result (`impl Fn(..) -> bool`), so mirroring Bevy means stating it. |
| Sites | `epix_engine/pbr/include/epix/pbr/cluster.hpp` (`extract_view_clusters`); `epix_engine/pbr/include/epix/pbr/light_cluster.hpp` (`estimate_cluster_index_count`, `limit_clusterable_objects_for_uniform_buffer`, `cached_cluster_sphere`) |
| Also fixed | Both headers stated those constraints while relying on transitive includes for `<concepts>` and `<type_traits>`; both now include them. |
| Sweep | A scan of all six audited modules (headers **and** sources) for `EPIX_EXPORT` within five lines after a `template<` head now reports **0** remaining. |
| Verification | Engine build `BUILD=0`; whole-tree build green (`-j4`; the `-j8` attempt hit C1060 compiler heap exhaustion, a resource limit, not a code error); ctest 98/99, the single failure being the render-module `GpuArrayBuffer.SelectsBackingAndIndexes`, which **passes in isolation in 3.1 s** and is the known load-sensitive flake; `tests_header_pbr_cluster_tests`, which had failed with `0xc0000139` (`STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND`) from binaries left stale by an aborted experiment, passes after relinking; 53-example sweep at its baseline; captures `DBABB1D0…` and `E7B7E7ED…` byte-identical. |
| Parent modules touched | none — `bevy_pbr` only. |
| Status | **committed as `cf7834d3`** |
| Note | The lesson generalises beyond this file: the port states constraints in several places, and a constraint that only checks invocability is documentation that cannot fail. The scan above is the check for the first half of the defect; the result-type half has to be read function by function, since only the body says what the callable's value is used for. |

### Batch 87 — the generator's field regex dropped every pointer field

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Mismatch IDs | none — a defect in the WebGPU wrapper's generator, outside the six modules but fixed with the user's explicit direction |
| What was wrong | `libs/webgpu-wrapper/generate.py`'s `field_re` was `r"^\s*(.+) (\w+);$"`, which requires a literal space before the field name. Every pointer field in the current wgpu-native headers is written `Type const *name;`, so it matched **nothing** and the field was dropped silently: proved with the regex itself, `('WGPUBuffer const *', 'buffers')` for the spaced form and no match for the compact one. |
| Consequence | `wgpu::BindGroupEntryExtras` was generated with its three count fields and none of the `SmallVec` arrays or `setTextureViews`/`setSamplers`/`setBuffers` setters, so the port had **no way to express a binding array** — which is what blocked `PBR-319`, and what batch 82 wrongly attributed to the wrapper's design. |
| Change | `field_re = re.compile(r"^\s*(.+?)\s*(\w+);$")` — the type/name split is left to the trailing identifier, so `*name` and `* name` both parse. |
| Files | `libs/webgpu-wrapper/generate.py` (submodule commit `bde51cc`), engine commit `707206c2` for the pointer |
| Verification | Generated from the build's own configured inputs (the wgpu-native release `webgpu.h` + `wgpu.h`): the extras now emit `setBuffers`/`setSamplers`/`setTextureViews` and the `SmallVec` members, and their `to_cstruct` writes the pointers with their counts. Whole-tree build green against the regenerated wrapper (`audit-full-genfix.log`); CTest reached **98/99** before stalling on its last test under load and was stopped. |
| Parent modules touched | none directly; the regenerated wrapper is a build artifact, and `build/…/generated/webgpu` was refreshed so it is no longer stale. |
| Status | **committed as `707206c2`** (submodule `bde51cc`) |
| Note | This is the second time a plausible mechanism for `PBR-319` was wrong in the *diagnosis* rather than the attempt; the difference here is that the disproof is a two-line regex test anyone can repeat, and the fix is one line. |

### Batch 105 — the GPU instance builder's `update`

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Mismatch IDs | `PBR-165`, `PBR-166`, `PBR-167` — code ported, all three **left open** pending the driving test |
| Bevy behaviour | `RenderMeshInstanceGpuBuilder::update` (`render/mesh.rs:1128-1262`): resolve the vertex and index slices, the skin byte offset, the material binding and the lightmap; build the `MeshInputUniform`; then either keep a present entity's uniform slot and hand its old uniform to the previous frame's buffer, or take a new slot. |
| Port details worth naming | `u32::MAX` stands for "no skin" and `u16::MAX` for "no lightmap", as Bevy writes them; `index_count` takes the *vertex* count for a non-indexed mesh; the material slot and lightmap slot are packed into one word (low and high 16 bits); the world matrix is stored transposed; and the frame number is the timestamp that makes the injection pass able to validate the previous transform. The unprepared-material path is Bevy's: queue the entity for re-extraction next frame and write nothing, rather than drawing with a stale binding. |
| Structural notes | `MeshesToReextractNextFrame` is declared in the header and defined later in the same file, so the builder's declaration carries a forward declaration and the definition is reached through its `operator->`, which is the port's `Deref`. The instance's world-space centre is computed here because the builder does not carry one. |
| Test owed | The only input that needs a device is `MeshAllocator`, whose constructor is private and reached through `from_world` - so the driving test needs the GPU harness rather than being device-free like the material registry's. That is the next step; the three rows stay open until it exists, which is the same rule applied to `PBR-317`. |

### Batch 106 — the builder `update`'s driving test, closing three rows

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Mismatch IDs | `PBR-165`, `PBR-166`, `PBR-167` (❌ → ✅) |
| Test | `MeshInstance.BuilderUpdateWritesTheUniformAndKeepsTheSlot` runs the builder on a device with a prepared material, a lightmap, no skin and no mesh allocation, then again for the same entity, then once more for an entity whose material is not in the bindings. |
| What it pins | The uniform's rules: the `u32::MAX` skin sentinel, zero slices for an unallocated mesh, the frame as the timestamp, the tag, the material slot in the low half and lightmap slot in the high half of one word, and the *transposed* world matrix. The instance record: its uniform index, its world-space centre (the local centre through the model matrix, whose translation is four along x - hence five), and its resolved material slot and lightmap slab. The occupied arm: the same entity keeps the slot its previous uniform lives at, and its old uniform moves into the previous-frame buffer, which is what motion vectors read. And the bail-out: an unprepared material writes nothing, leaves the entity out of the instances map, and queues it for re-extraction. |
| Build notes worth keeping | Two things had to be fixed that only the compiler links can reveal: the builder's `update` is a member defined in a `.cpp`, so `RenderMeshInstanceGpuBuilder` needs `EPIX_API` on the class or the symbol is not exported (the same rule the light-cluster structs taught); and a brace-initialised `glm::vec3`/`glm::uvec2` inside an `EXPECT_EQ` breaks the macro on its commas, so such values are hoisted into named locals. |
| Why this test needed a device | `MeshAllocator`'s constructor is private and reached through `from_world`, so unlike the material registry this could not be verified as plain data. That was recorded in the previous batch rather than discovered again here. |
| Verification | Whole-tree build green; CTest **104/104** at `-j3`; `mesh_rendering` `DBABB1D0…` byte-identical. |
| Parent modules touched | none. |

Ranked by value from the sections merged so far:

1. **Tracker maintenance, second half**: re-derive `mesh-mesh_rs.md`'s ~91 `mesh.hpp` citations by content. `mesh-lead-verified.md`'s eight were done in batch 40 and each was verified by reading the cited line; automation was tried for the rest and rejected — the symbols collide with doc-comment mentions, parameters and `spdlog` messages, and a dry run (`tmp/audit/fix-mesh-citations*.ps1`) proposed wrong targets for a tenth of the rows — so this is a per-row, by-hand pass. `tmp/audit/check-prose.ps1` covers status labels and counts, not line numbers; the check is a per-row read of the entity and a `grep` for it.
2. The rest of the 3D mesh pipeline's instance side — `PBR-181` (`set_mesh_motion_vector_flags`, the only writer of `HAS_PREVIOUS_SKIN`/`HAS_PREVIOUS_MORPH`, so motion vectors cannot be flagged without it) and `PBR-182`/`PBR-183` (`collect_meshes_for_gpu_building`, whose `previous_input_buffer.ensure_nonempty()` is what makes the previous-input binding valid), then the CPU extraction path (`PBR-173`..`PBR-175`) — the bulk of the pbr module's remaining ❌ rows; both halves need the material pipeline and the skinning/morph resources, which are unported.
3. The rest of the mesh pipeline's construction, in dependency order: the view-layout half (`MeshPipelineViewLayouts`, `MeshPipelineViewLayout`, `generate_view_layouts` in `mesh_view_bindings.rs`, `PBR-271` plus the rows to add, and the `MESH_PIPELINE_VIEW_LAYOUT_SAFE_MAX_TEXTURES` debug guard `PBR-103`), then the runtime bind group constructors (`PBR-269`, `PBR-270`), then `MeshPipeline` itself with its `specialize` and the mesh shaders (`PBR-184`..`PBR-195`, `PBR-238`/`PBR-239`, `PBR-242`, `PBR-254`..`PBR-256`). `MeshLayouts` is done (batch 38), so are the prepass (batch 41), light-probe (batch 43), clustered-decal (batch 46) and screen-space-reflection (batch 48) pieces, the OIT settings and support check (batch 47) and the cluster buffers' minimum sizes (batch 44); the view layouts (batch 50), three shader modules (batch 51) and the `MeshPipeline` resource itself (batch 52) are done. The shader side now has seven of the nine modules in `PBR-262`'s set, plus the view types and bindings, all compile-checked. What remains before a 3D mesh can be drawn is the runtime path around `specialize`: the lightmap and skin resources the batching adapter needs (`RenderLightmaps`, `SkinUniforms`) together with that adapter (`PBR-199`..`PBR-201`), then the mesh and view bind groups (`PBR-269`/`PBR-270`, `PBR-301`/`PBR-302`), and the forward chain (`pbr_functions`, `pbr_lighting`, `shadows`, `clustered_forward`, `fog`) that material shaders need. The mesh bind groups are ported apart from the lightmapped one and the two binding-array entries (`PBR-269`, `PBR-319`), and pbr's remaining headers still inline their implementations — that cleanup comes next — assembling those entries into the phase's `BindGroup`s against the mesh buffers, the skin uniforms and the lightmaps, all of which now exist — together with the two binding-array entries (`PBR-319`). What a live 3D mesh still needs beyond that: the writers that populate the lightmap and skin data (`PBR-315`, `PBR-317`), the view bind groups (`PBR-301`/`PBR-302`), the phase queueing that calls the adapter, and the forward chain for material shaders. Then `specialize` (`PBR-238`/`PBR-239`/`PBR-242`, `PBR-254`..`PBR-256`) and the runtime bind groups (`PBR-269`/`PBR-270`, `PBR-301`/`PBR-302`).
4. `CGR-208`, `CGR-218`, `CGR-226`, `CGR-294`, `CGR-301` — the render diagnostics and `trace` spans absent from every pass node: Bevy's spans need a diagnostics facility Epix does not have, and its `info_span!`s have no Epix counterpart either (Tracy is wired only into `app`/`ecs`), so this needs a facility row before the nodes can follow.
5. `PBR-149`'s `Parallel<T>` — one queue per thread is the last shape gap in the queue resource and the prerequisite for a parallel extraction.
6. `SRD-426`, `SRD-366` — both blocked on facilities or decisions (`Handle::default()`, Bevy's fallible `SRes`).

## Parent-module divergences

Every row whose section marked it `PARENT:` in its difference cell, plus every non-✅ row whose **Entity** or **Epix** cell carries the marker — a divergence that belongs to a parent module (`render`, `pbr`, `assets`, `camera`, `transform`, …) or to a subsystem Epix does not have, rather than to the audited module itself. The three rows a section marked `PARENT:` in the Entity cell *and* graded ✅ (`PBR-851`, `PBR-852`, `PBR-853`) are coverage evidence and stay in their merged section only. Fixing any of these requires the parent module to be audited and the user to approve before committing (see `_policy.md`, "Commits").

## Audited sections

The twelve section files merged verbatim, in this order, each under a `<!-- section: … -->` marker: mesh (Lead-verified first, then `mesh.rs`), image (`image.rs` first, then the loader/conversion/atlas/decoder files), sprite (core first, then `text2d`/picking), sprite_render (the sprite render path first, then `mesh2d`/`material2d`/`color_material`/`wireframe2d`/`text2d`/`tilemap_chunk`), core_graph (core_3d/core_2d first, then the rest of `bevy_core_pipeline`), pbr (`render/mesh.rs` first, then the `bevy_light`/`light.rs`/`cluster.rs`/`components.rs` set). Nothing inside them is rewritten, renumbered, reordered or summarised — they are the evidence behind every row above.

Numbered non-✅ rows:

1. `MSH-100` (🚫) — `INDEX_BUFFER_ASSET_INDEX` absent from Epix (dead inside Bevy 0.18: no reader anywhere in `crates/`).
2. `MSH-101` (🚫) — `VERTEX_ATTRIBUTE_BUFFER_ID` absent from Epix (also unused inside Bevy 0.18).
3. `MSH-112` (⚠️) — `impl From<Option<T>> for MeshExtractableData<T>` has no named Epix counterpart; folded into `replace(std::optional<T>)` plus the `data()` factory.
4. `MSH-113` (⚠️) — `Mesh` type: Epix derives no `Reflect`/`Asset`; registration is done by `MeshPlugin::attach`, and the copy constructor must be hand-maintained to preserve per-payload extracted state.
5. `MSH-130` (⚠️) — `Mesh::try_attribute_data` (crate-private accessor for the whole `MeshAttributeData`) has no counterpart; Epix `merge` rebuilds the descriptor through `MeshAttributeLayout` (a full map copy).
6. *(MSH-159 ✅ fixed in `9c537148` — the topology guard is an always-on precondition now.)*
7. *(MSH-161 ✅ fixed in `9c537148` — all three flat-normal guards too.)*
8. *(MSH-167 ✅ fixed in `9c537148` — always-on guards plus bounds-checked faces in the built-in callbacks.)*
9. `MSH-172` (🚫) — `Mesh::generate_tangents` (feature `bevy_mikktspace`) has no Epix equivalent at all.
10. `MSH-173` (🚫) — `Mesh::with_generated_tangents` (feature `bevy_mikktspace`) has no Epix equivalent at all.
11. `MSH-187` (⚠️) — Epix triangle iteration holds raw pointers into the mesh, so `MeshTriangles` can outlive its mesh where Bevy's `+ '_` borrow prevents it.
12. `MSH-198` (🚫) — `impl Mul<Mesh> for Transform` has no Epix counterpart (only the `transformed_by` method exists).
13. `MSH-200` (⚠️) — `SerializedMesh::from_mesh`: Bevy `unwrap()`s the replaced `Option<BTreeMap>` (panic); Epix dereferences the empty optional (UB) — only reachable if attributes are `NoData`.
14. *(MSH-218 ✅ ported in `ee9f4bee` — `Triangle3d::normal` returns `std::expected<Dir3, InvalidDirectionError>`, with `Dir3` and the error added beside it in `mesh/direction.hpp`.)*
15. `MSH-223` (⚠️) — `MeshAttributeLayout` is an Epix-only type (no counterpart anywhere in `crates/`).
16. `MSH-234` (⚠️) — `MeshPlugin`: Epix misses Bevy's `register_asset_reflect::<Mesh>()` and does not attach `MorphPlugin` (the morph system lives in the morph module).

# Bevy `bevy_image/src/image.rs` — entity-level parity audit (IMG-100..IMG-269)

Bevy reference: tag `v0.18.0`, commit `5f8270f2e049f90139a503d1e930070d926f9427`, at `tmp/bevy-0.18.0`.

**Bevy files read:**
- `bevy_image/src/image.rs` — the brief said ~2260 lines, the file on disk is **2410** lines; read in full (imports at 1-27 through the `mod test` at 2125-2410).
- `bevy_image/src/image_texture_conversion.rs:1-200` — only the two bodies `Image::convert` calls (`from_dynamic` 9-162, `try_into_dynamic` 173-200); the rest of that file is another section's scope.

## Not audited

- `bevy_image/src/image_loader.rs` (`ImageLoader`, `ImageLoaderSettings`, `ImageFormatSetting`, `ImageArrayLayout`, `ImageLoaderError`) and `image_texture_conversion.rs` beyond the two `convert` callees — separate sections of this tracker.
- `bevy_image/src/{basis,dds,ktx2}.rs`, `compressed_image_saver.rs`, `serialized_image.rs`, `image_saver` plumbing.
- `epix_engine/render/render/**`: `GpuImage`/`RenderAsset<Image>` preparation, sampler creation from `as_wgpu`, `create_texture_with_data` row padding and upload ordering, `fallback_image.hpp`, `screenshot.cpp` — all `PARENT: render`. Their only contact points judged here are IMG-110, IMG-161, IMG-253, IMG-264.
- `epix_engine/image/src/image_loader.cpp` was read only in the regions that back this file's rows (`from_buffer`, `load`, `save`, `to_string`, `SUPPORTED_FORMATS`, `extensions`); the decoder, loader settings resolution and array-layout stages are the `image_loader.rs` section's scope.
- `epix_engine/image/src/texture_atlas.cpp`, `atlas_allocator.cpp`, `rectangle_pack.cpp` and `texture_atlas.hpp` — unrelated to `image.rs`.
- Test bodies were used as evidence of intent (`image_parity_tests.cpp` was read around the sampler/size/resize/colour-accessor tests and inventoried by name); the loader, atlas and pack suites were not read.
- The wgpu-types crate was consulted for `TextureFormat`/`Extent3d`/`TextureDataOrder` only; no other dependency (`bevy_color`'s `Srgba`/`Xyza`/`LinearRgba` conversions) was opened, so the sRGB transfer function and luminance coefficients in IMG-221/222 are compared against Epix's own comments plus the known constants, not against `bevy_color` sources.

# Bevy `bevy_image` loader / conversion / atlas section — entity-level parity audit (IMG-300..IMG-538)

Bevy reference: tag `v0.18.0`, commit `5f8270f2e049f90139a503d1e930070d926f9427`, at `tmp/bevy-0.18.0`.

This section covers `image_loader.rs`, `image_texture_conversion.rs`, `lib.rs`, `serialized_image.rs`,
`compressed_image_saver.rs`, `texture_atlas.rs`, `texture_atlas_builder.rs`,
`dynamic_texture_atlas_builder.rs` and the five format files (`ktx2.rs`, `basis.rs`, `dds.rs`,
`exr_texture_loader.rs`, `hdr_texture_loader.rs`).

It owns the entities the sibling `image.rs` section deferred: IMG-266 (`ImageFormatSetting` /
`ImageArrayLayout` / `ImageLoaderSettings`), IMG-267 (`PixelBuffer` / `DynamicImage` /
`IntoDynamicImageError`), IMG-268 (`Image::from_dynamic`), IMG-269 (`Image::try_into_dynamic`) —
they are audited here as IMG-308..IMG-320, IMG-351, IMG-340..IMG-345 and IMG-346..IMG-350.
`bevy_image/src/image.rs` itself (IMG-100..IMG-269) is **not** re-audited; where a row's body lives
there it is cited as a dependency of the row, not re-decided.

**Bevy files read:**
- `bevy_image/src/image_loader.rs` (248 lines, in full), `image_texture_conversion.rs` (244, in full),
  `lib.rs` (57, in full), `serialized_image.rs` (178, in full), `compressed_image_saver.rs` (78, in
  full), `texture_atlas.rs` (246, in full), `texture_atlas_builder.rs` (302, in full),
  `dynamic_texture_atlas_builder.rs` (129, in full), `exr_texture_loader.rs` (80, in full),
  `hdr_texture_loader.rs` (79, in full), `basis.rs` (169, in full).
- `bevy_image/src/ktx2.rs` (1518 lines) and `dds.rs` (410): declaration surface and headers read;
  bodies **not** read line-by-line, because Epix has no counterpart for either file (see IMG-509..).
- `bevy_image/Cargo.toml:11-49` and `bevy_internal/Cargo.toml:36-56` — the feature gates that decide
  `ImageLoader::SUPPORTED_FORMATS`.

Epix has **no counterpart** for this file: `basis-universal` is not vendored
(`epix_engine/image/CMakeLists.txt:9` links `stbimage` only) and no `AssetSaver` for `Image` is
registered. `Image::save` (image_loader.cpp:484-531) is an Epix-only filesystem writer, not the
asset-processor saver Bevy models (recorded as IMG-255).

### bevy_image/src/ktx2.rs

Epix has **no counterpart** for this file. Its public functions are reached by `Image::from_buffer`
(image.rs:1386) and its extensions are advertised by `ImageLoader::SUPPORTED_FORMATS`; in Epix
`is_decodable(Ktx2)` is false (image.cpp:562-581), `ktx2` is absent from `SUPPORTED_FORMATS`
(image_loader.cpp:539-542) and a `.ktx2` asset reports `UnsupportedTextureFormat{"Ktx2"}`
(image_loader_tests.cpp:352-360). The only KTX2 parsing in the tree is the narrow, level-0-only,
Zstd-supercompressed LUT decoder in `render/core_graph/src/tonemapping.cpp:324-430`, which is a
different module with a different purpose (`PARENT: render/core_graph`) and is **not** a loader.
Rows IMG-509..IMG-517 therefore record missing entities only; no Epix-side code is detailed.

`UnsupportedTextureFormat{"OpenExr"}` (image_loader_tests.cpp:362-373). Unlike `.hdr`, there is no
equivalent path inside `ImageLoader` — `stb_image` cannot read EXR at all.

### bevy_image/src/hdr_texture_loader.rs

Epix has a **functional but not structural** counterpart: `.hdr` is decoded by `ImageLoader`
(`SUPPORTED_FORMATS` includes `Hdr`, image_loader.cpp:539-542) through `stb_image`'s float path
(image_loader.cpp:244-250) and `Image::from_dynamic`'s `Rgb32F` arm. There is no separate loader type,
settings type or error enum, so the type-shaped rows are ⚠️/🚫 and the behaviour-shaped rows are ✅.

# Bevy `bevy_sprite/src/text2d.rs` + `bevy_sprite/src/picking_backend.rs` — entity-level parity audit (SPR-400..SPR-435)

Bevy reference: tag `v0.18.0` at `tmp/bevy-0.18.0`.

**Bevy files:**
- `bevy_sprite/src/text2d.rs` — brief said 434 lines, file on disk is **479** lines; read in full.
- `bevy_sprite/src/picking_backend.rs` — brief said 264 lines, file on disk is **292** lines; read in full.

**Epix files read:**
- `epix_engine/text/include/epix/text/render.hpp` (180) — `Text2d`, `Text2dBundle`, `TextRenderPlugin`, `extract_text2d_layout`.
- `epix_engine/text/src/render.cpp` (142) — `Text2d::on_add`, required components, `extract_text2d_sprite`, `calculate_bounds_text2d`.
- `epix_engine/text/include/epix/text/text.hpp` (292) — `Text`, `TextFont`, `TextLayout`, `TextBounds`, `ShapedText`, `GlyphInfo`, `TextColor`.
- `epix_engine/text/src/text.cpp` (499) — `shape_changed_text`, `shape_text`, `TextPlugin::attach`.
- `epix_engine/text/tests/header/text_render_path.cpp` (186).
- `epix_engine/sprite/include/epix/sprite/sprite.hpp` (156), `epix_engine/sprite/src/sprite.cpp` (185), `epix_engine/sprite/include/epix/sprite/texture_slice.hpp` (86), `epix_engine/sprite/src/texture_slice.cpp` (lines 1–60).
- `epix_engine/sprite_render/include/epix/sprite_render/render.hpp` (454), `epix_engine/sprite_render/src/render.cpp` (757), `epix_engine/sprite_render/include/epix/sprite_render/material2d.hpp` (496).
- Searched (not read in full): `epix_engine/text/include/epix/text/font.hpp`, `epix_engine/camera/src/camera.cpp`, `epix_engine/camera/include/epix/camera/visibility.hpp`, `epix_engine/ecs/**`, `epix_engine/input/**`, `epix_engine/image/**`, `epix_engine/window/**`.
- Prior records consulted: `tmp/audit/_policy.md`, `tmp/tracker-text-rows.md`, `tmp/g22/track_head.md` (row S8).

**Picking conclusion:** Epix has **no picking backend of any kind**. A tree-wide search of `epix_engine` for `SpritePicking`, `bevy_picking`, `Pickable`, `PointerHits`, `HitData`, `PickingSystems` and `pointer_location` returns zero matches, and there is no `picking` module/target. Epix input stops at raw device events (`MouseMove`, `MouseScroll`, `MouseButtonInput`, `epix_engine/input/include/epix/input/events.hpp:26-40`); there is no `PointerId`/`PointerLocation`/`RayMap`/`HitData`/`Pickable` abstraction. This is already recorded as missing by `tmp/g22/track_head.md` row S8; SPR-424..SPR-435 below are the entity-level breakdown.

## Summary

Counts: **✅ 3**, **❌ 0**, **⚠️ 18**, **🚫 14**, **⛔ 1**, **REVIEW 0** — 36 rows.
(The two rows fixed since this section was written are `SPR-418` in `835053d7` and the required-component half of `SPR-400`, which now carries its own ⚠️.)

Classification rule used here: ⚠️ marks an entity that is absent or reshaped but whose divergence is **explicitly recorded as knowingly deferred, with a rationale**, in `tmp/tracker-text-rows.md` item (4)/(5) (text spans, `Text2dShadow`, `FontHinting`, `LineHeight`, DPI scale factor, `Text2d::offset`, `TextMeasure`); 🚫 marks an absence with no such record. The two ❌ rows are not covered by that record and are actionable.

Non-✅ IDs:

1. SPR-400 ⚠️ — `Text2d` now requires `TextFont`, `TextLayout` and `TextBounds` (commit `835053d7`), so a bare entity is queryable and shapeable; `LineHeight`/`FontHinting::Disabled` still have no Epix component, and the required `TextFont` carries an invalid handle because Epix has no default-font asset convention.
2. SPR-401 ✅, SPR-419 ✅ (listed for coverage: the `on_add` hook and the AABB arithmetic match Bevy exactly).
3. SPR-402 ⚠️ — `Text2d` carries no `String`; content lives on the separate `Text` component and `Text2d` adds an `offset` extension.
4. SPR-403 ⚠️ — no `Text2d::new`; content is built by `Text::with_str`.
5. SPR-404 ⚠️ — no `TextRoot`; no `ComputedTextBlock`/span hierarchy.
6. SPR-405 ⚠️ — no `TextSpanAccess`.
7. SPR-406 ⚠️ — no `read_span`.
8. SPR-407 ⚠️ — no `write_span`.
9. SPR-408 ⚠️ — no `From<&str> for Text2d`.

## Summary

Counts: ✅ 183 · ❌ 0 · ⚠️ 12 · 🚫 0 · ⛔ 1 · REVIEW 1 (total 197 rows, SRD-100..SRD-296).
(SRD-216 was fixed in commit `ddc844a4`; see `## Fix batches` in the tracker.)

Non-✅ rows:

1. **SRD-101** ⚠️ — no C++ `prelude` module; the umbrella header `epix/sprite_render.hpp` exports `ColorMaterial`/`MeshMaterial2d` (plus the rest of the crate).
2. **SRD-107** ⚠️ — `Plugin::build` is split into `attach` (main world) + `ready` (render world), the repo-wide plugin lifecycle convention.
3. **SRD-109** ⚠️ — `load_shader_library!(sprite_view_bindings.wgsl)` has no counterpart: Epix declares the view bindings inside the one sprite Slang asset.
4. **SRD-110** ⚠️ — the embedded sprite shader is a single Slang asset (`sprite/sprite.slang`) registered through `EmbeddedAssetRegistry` in `attach`; registration is silently skipped if the registry/asset server is absent (Bevy's `embedded_asset!` would panic).
5. **SRD-118** REVIEW — Epix adds `SyncComponentPlugin<Sprite>` (required component **plus** component-removed render-world cleanup) where Bevy registers only the required component; whether the extra cleanup is intended could not be confirmed.
6. **SRD-124** ⛔ — `extract_text2d_sprite` (cfg `bevy_text`) belongs to the text2d section.
7. **SRD-125** ⚠️ — `ambiguous_with(queue_material2d_meshes::<ColorMaterial>)` has no Epix counterpart; Epix has no ambiguity-reporting subsystem (the declaration is diagnostic-only in Bevy, schedule order is unordered in both).
8. **SRD-155** ⚠️ — Bevy's `TONEMAPPING_LUT_TEXTURE_BINDING_INDEX`/`_SAMPLER_` uint shader defs are unnecessary in Epix, which declares the LUT bindings at fixed Slang locations and passes them to `tone_mapping`.
9. *(SRD-195 ✅ fixed in `555a8702` — the Epix-only `CustomRendered` marker and its `Without<>` filter are gone, so a marked sprite is extracted the way Bevy extracts it.)*
10. *(SRD-216 ✅ fixed in `ddc844a4` — the system is `queue_sprites`.)*
11. **SRD-252** ⚠️ — a missing image bind group returns `RenderCommandError::Failure` in Epix where Bevy `unwrap()`s; same fatal outcome, Epix's error-return convention.
12. **SRD-255** ⚠️ — unprepared sprite buffers return `Failure` instead of Bevy's two `unwrap()` panics; same fatal outcome.
13. **SRD-257** ⚠️ — no `bevy_sprite::sprite_view_bindings` module (`#define_import_path`); the bindings are merged into the sprite Slang file.
14. **SRD-263** ⚠️ — `sprite.wgsl`'s `#import bevy_sprite::sprite_view_bindings` has no import target; the bindings are inlined (see SRD-257).
15. **SRD-265** ⚠️ — `@builtin(vertex_index)` is replaced by Slang `SV_VulkanVertexID` (raw Vulkan index; `SV_VertexID` would pull in `BaseVertex`/`DrawParameters`); identical while `base_vertex` is 0, as documented in the Epix comment.
16. **SRD-290** ⚠️ — `SpriteImageMode::Auto`/`Scale` reach `unreachable!()` in Bevy but return `nullopt` in Epix; unreachable in practice (both callers gate on `uses_slices()`).

Decisions for the Lead: (a) whether the extra render-world cleanup from `SyncComponentPlugin<Sprite>` is intended (SRD-118); (b) whether to rename `queue_sprites_2d` (SRD-216, since renamed). The `CustomRendered` question (SRD-195) is settled: the Lead chose Bevy's behaviour, so the marker and its filter were removed in `555a8702`.

- Entity detail of `Mesh2dRenderPlugin`, `ColorMaterialPlugin`, `TilemapChunkPlugin`, `TilemapChunkMaterialPlugin` (SRD-112..SRD-115) and of `Material2dPlugin<ColorMaterial>` / `queue_material2d_meshes` — only their registration by `SpriteRenderPlugin` and the ambiguity declaration are covered here; the Epix `material2d.hpp/.cpp` entity detail belongs to the material2d section.
- Bodies of the imported Bevy shader modules (`bevy_render::maths`, `bevy_render::view::View`, `bevy_core_pipeline::tonemapping`) and of the corresponding Epix Slang modules (`epix.view`, `epix.tonemapping`) — out of scope; only the sprite-side call sites and binding slots were compared.
- Bevy `bevy_sprite` crate entities used by this path (`Sprite`, `Anchor`, `SpriteScalingMode`, `TextureSlice`, `SpriteImageMode`, `TextureAtlasLayout`) and the Epix counterparts in `epix_engine/sprite/**` — out of scope for this section.

Two consequences: (a) whether Epix's `attach`-time embedded-shader registration always precedes the render-world `RenderStartup` load was reasoned from the plugin lifecycle, not observed; (b) entry-point naming (`vs_main`/`fs_main` vs Bevy's defaulted `vertex`/`fragment`) was compared from source only.

## Summary

Counts: **✅ 258**, **❌ 1**, **⚠️ 14**, **🚫 3**, **⛔ 0**, **REVIEW 1** — 277 rows, SRD-300..SRD-575 plus the `PRT-3` parent row.
(SRD-414 and SRD-415 were fixed in `e95d0269`, SRD-305/SRD-330 in `555a8702`, SRD-399/SRD-457 in `18c9af19` and the `PRT-3` parent row in `90ac9a0f`; see `## Fix batches` in the tracker.)

Classification notes: (a) Slang-vs-WGSL is the recorded project convention and is not itself a mismatch — each shader row states whether the maths/bindings are equivalent, and the WGSL→Slang matrix-orientation compensation in `ColorMaterialUniform::uv_transform` and `Mesh2dUniform::world_from_local` was re-derived against `bevy_render/src/maths.wgsl` and found equivalent. (b) Missing 2D-text features that `tmp/tracker-text-rows.md` item (4) already records as deliberately deferred (spans/per-span colours, `Text2dShadow`, `Underline`/`Strikethrough`/`TextBackgroundColor`, `TextLayoutInfo::scale_factor`) are marked ⚠️, matching the classification rule the sibling section used. (c) The sibling section (`sprite_render-render.md`) already enumerated `texture_slice/mod.rs` + `computed_slices.rs` as SRD-279..SRD-296, so those files get no rows here (see *Not audited*).

Non-✅ rows:

1. *(SRD-305 ✅ fixed in `555a8702` — the CPU instance-buffer writer takes only the adapter now, the phase plugins register batch/sweep/sort systems only, and mesh2d keeps its single registration where Bevy's is, so the shared `BatchedInstanceBuffer<Mesh2dUniform>` is uploaded once.)*
2. *(SRD-330 ✅ fixed in `555a8702` — the Epix-only `CustomRendered` marker and its `Without<>` filter are gone, so `extract_mesh2d` queries exactly Bevy's items.)*
3. **SRD-366** REVIEW — `SetMesh2dBindGroup` takes a non-optional `Res<Mesh2dBindGroup>` where Bevy's `SRes` failure is an in-item error+skip; whether Epix's param-validation policy (render-core, `render_phase.hpp:626-633` throws) is intended could not be decided here.
4. **SRD-379** ⚠️ — `MeshMaterial2d::default()` has no usable Epix counterpart because `assets::Handle<T>` deletes its default constructor (`handle.hpp:89`), so there is no "default material" handle.
5. *(SRD-399 ✅ fixed in `18c9af19` — both copies of the command return `Skip` when the material instance or the prepared material is missing.)*
6. *(SRD-414 ✅ fixed in `e95d0269` — the opaque bin key now carries the mesh asset id.)*
7. *(SRD-415 ✅ fixed in `e95d0269` — the alpha-mask bin key too.)*
8. **SRD-417** ⚠️ — `Material2dBindGroupId` carries the material asset id instead of a `BindGroupId` (direct wgpu has none); documented in the Epix header, but coarser than Bevy's identity.
9. **SRD-421** ⚠️ — `PreparedMaterial2d::get_bind_group_id()` has no Epix counterpart; the queue derives the id from the instance map instead.
10. **SRD-426** ❌ — `ColorMaterialPlugin` inserts the default magenta material at a freshly allocated index; Bevy inserts at `Handle::<ColorMaterial>::default()`, so Bevy's default material handle resolves and Epix's does not (Epix's own `DEFAULT_IMAGE_HANDLE` shows the intended pattern).
11. **SRD-435** 🚫 — `impl From<Handle<Image>> for ColorMaterial` is missing from Epix.
12. *(SRD-457 ✅ fixed in `18c9af19` — the writer carries a `Res<Wireframe2dConfig>` change condition, so it no longer re-marks the global material every frame.)*
13. **SRD-477** ⚠️ — the node now logs the phase's `DrawError` inside its deferred command-buffer task with Bevy's wording (the parent phase API landed as PRT-3 in `90ac9a0f`); it cannot return `NodeRunError::DrawError` because that task has no error channel and Epix's `NodeRunError` carries no payload. The propagation half needs the render module's encoder model to match Bevy's per-node split.
14. **SRD-513** ⚠️ — Bevy's extractor multiplies by `GlobalTransform::from_scale(scale_factor.recip())`; Epix has no `TextLayoutInfo::scale_factor` (recorded deferral), so HiDPI text is laid out at scale 1.
15. **SRD-515** ⚠️ — `TextBackgroundColor` run rectangles are not emitted (recorded deferral).
16. **SRD-516** ⚠️ — the `Text2dShadow` glyph-slice path is not implemented (recorded deferral).
17. **SRD-517** ⚠️ — the shadow's strikethrough/underline sprites are not implemented (recorded deferral).
18. **SRD-519** ⚠️ — the sprite run is flushed on atlas-texture change only; Bevy also flushes on `span_index` change (single-span text, recorded deferral).
19. **SRD-520** ⚠️ — per-span `TextColor` resolution is absent; Epix applies one entity-level colour (recorded deferral).
20. **SRD-521** ⚠️ — the main-path strikethrough/underline decorations are not emitted (recorded deferral).
21. **SRD-522** ⚠️ — Bevy `unwrap()`s a missing atlas layout/index; Epix skips the glyph (Epix's error-return convention, same class as the sibling's SRD-252/255/290).
22. **SRD-528** ⚠️ — `TilemapChunk` is only conventionally immutable in Epix; Bevy declares `#[component(immutable)]`, so post-insert mutation cannot be expressed there.
23. **SRD-571** 🚫 — `mesh2d_functions::mesh2d_position_local_to_clip` is missing from the Epix shader (Bevy keeps the intermediate `world_position` for precision).
24. **SRD-574** 🚫 — `mesh2d_functions::get_tag` is missing, and Epix's mesh2d helper functions are module-private rather than a shared shader library, so a material shader cannot reuse them at all.
25. **SRD-575** ⚠️ — Bevy's five mesh2d WGSL libraries collapse into one private Slang asset (`sprite/mesh2d.slang`); recorded in the Epix comment, but it is the reason SRD-571/574 cannot be reached by user shaders.

Decisions for the Lead: (a) whether Epix wants a default-asset-handle convention for `ColorMaterial` (SRD-426) or accepts the missing default material. The rest are settled: the bin-key `asset_id` defect (SRD-414/415) was fixed in `e95d0269`, and the Lead chose Bevy's behaviour for both `CustomRendered` questions (SRD-330 and the sibling's SRD-195) and for the duplicate instance-buffer writer (SRD-305), so `555a8702` removed the filter and left one writer, registered by the pipeline plugin.

## Not audited

- `bevy_sprite_render/src/texture_slice/mod.rs` and `texture_slice/computed_slices.rs` — listed in this section's scope, but already enumerated entity-for-entity as **SRD-279..SRD-296** in `tmp/audit/sections/sprite_render-render.md` (that section read Epix `render.hpp:40-58` / `render.cpp:186-216,633-666` for them). No rows are re-issued here; the Epix code for those entities lives in `epix_engine/sprite_render/{include/epix/sprite_render/render.hpp,src/render.cpp}`, i.e. the sprite-render section's file, not the three `.cpp` files in this section's scope list.
- `bevy_sprite_render/src/lib.rs` `extract_text2d_sprite` registration and `ambiguous_with(...)` declaration — the sibling section owns them (SRD-124, SRD-125); only the ordering they impose is referenced here (SRD-511).
- Bodies of the imported shader modules: `bevy_render::view::View`, `bevy_render::globals::Globals`, `bevy_core_pipeline::tonemapping` and their Epix counterparts (`epix.view`, `epix.globals`, `epix.tonemapping`) — out of scope. `bevy_render/src/maths.wgsl` **was** read, because the correctness of `Mesh2dUniform`'s packing depends on `affine3_to_square`/`mat2x4_f32_to_mat3x3_unpack`.
- Bevy `bevy_text`/`bevy_sprite` text entities (`ComputedTextBlock`, `TextLayoutInfo`, `PositionedGlyph`, run geometry, `TextSpan`, `Text2dShadow`, `TextBounds`, `Anchor`, `Text2d`) and Epix `epix_engine/text/{include/epix/text/text.hpp,font.hpp}`, `text.cpp` — only the extractor's use of them was compared; `Text2d::offset`/`TextMeasure` (Epix extensions) belong to the sprite/text section.
- `epix_engine/render/render/**` and `epix_engine/render/core_graph/**` entities used as PARENT evidence (`RenderSystems` ordering, `BatchedInstanceBuffer`/`GpuArrayBuffer::write_buffer`, `BinnedRenderPhasePlugin`/`CpuBinnedRenderPhasePlugin`, `RenderCommand` param validation, `Transparent2D`/`Opaque2DBinKey`) — read only to judge scheduling and error-path equivalence; owned by the render/core_graph sections.
- Bevy `AsBindGroup` derive internals (`bevy_render/src/render_resource/as_bind_group.rs`) — only the declared binding attributes and Epix's hand-written `AsBindGroup` specializations were compared (SRD-448/449/556/557); the derive's own layout-entry visibility defaults were not read.
- Runtime verification: no build, test run, or GPU validation was performed (read-only audit). Two consequences: (a) whether Epix's `attach`-time shader registration always precedes the render-world load was reasoned from the plugin lifecycle, not observed; (b) the bind-group/skip paths (SRD-366, SRD-399) and the duplicate instance-buffer upload (SRD-305) were derived from source semantics, not from a capture.

# CGR-100..CGR-310 — bevy_core_pipeline core_3d / core_2d vs epix core_graph

Scope: Bevy `bevy_core_pipeline` Core3D (`core_3d/mod.rs` + its three pass nodes) and Core2D
(`core_2d/mod.rs` + its two pass nodes), entity by entity, against Epix
`epix_engine/render/core_graph/{include/epix/core_graph/core3d.hpp,core2d.hpp,src/core3d.cpp,core2d.cpp,copy_deferred_lighting_id.cpp}`
and the parent render module where an entity lives there (`PARENT: render`).

Bevy source pinned at `tmp/bevy-0.18.0/crates/`, tag `v0.18.0`, commit
`5f8270f2e049f90139a503d1e930070d926f9427` (verified with `git rev-parse HEAD` / `git describe --tags`).

**Line-number convention.** All Bevy/Epix line numbers are true file line numbers as reported by the
read tool. Note the brief's parenthesised sizes (`1122/127/146/93/443/93/103`) equal
`Get-Content | Measure-Object -Line`, which counts **non-blank** lines only; the true totals are
`1251/142/167/107/508/106/120`. Both sets describe the same pinned files.

**Label-string note (affects every node-label row).** The brief states Bevy node labels are
"strings … with `#[derive(RenderLabel)]`". That is not what the pinned source does:
`#[derive(RenderLabel)]` expands via `bevy_macro_utils::derive_label` to *only* `fn dyn_clone`
(`bevy_render/macros/src/lib.rs:81-92`, `bevy_macro_utils/src/label.rs:57-95`). There is no derived
label string; a label's identity is the interned `(concrete type, value)` pair
(`bevy_render/src/render_graph/node.rs:25-35`). So for the `Node3d`/`Node2d` enums the comparable
surface is: the label *type* name, the variant names, and their declaration order — all of which are
checked below (and `Node3d`/`Node2d` variant names/order match 1:1). See CGR-309/CGR-310.

- **Not executed**: no builds, tests, or GPU runs — every behavioural claim is source-derived. One claim of this kind was retracted during review: CGR-184 assumed the vendored C++ wrapper left `WGPUSamplerDescriptor` zero-initialised, but the generated default constructor applies wgpu-native's `WGPU_SAMPLER_DESCRIPTOR_INIT`, whose own values (`lodMaxClamp = 32.f`, `maxAnisotropy = 1`, `Undefined` enums that wgpu-native resolves to Rust's defaults) make Epix's minimal descriptor equivalent to Bevy's. Where a claim depends on third-party semantics, read the macro or crate source before grading the row; radsort's float ordering (CGR-157) is the remaining such claim.

# CGR-400..CGR-699 — `bevy_core_pipeline` minus `core_2d/**` / `core_3d/**`, entity by entity

Scope: everything in `bevy_core_pipeline` **except** `core_2d/**` and `core_3d/**` (owned by the
CGR-100..CGR-310 agent): `tonemapping/**`, `upscaling/**`, `blit/**`, `prepass/**`, `deferred/**`,
`skybox/**`, `oit/**`, `experimental/mip_generation/**`, `fullscreen_material.rs`,
`fullscreen_vertex_shader/**`, `lib.rs`.

Bevy source pinned at `tmp/bevy-0.18.0/crates/`, tag `v0.18.0`, commit
`5f8270f2e049f90139a503d1e930070d926f9427`. All line numbers are true file line numbers as reported
by the read tool (the brief's parenthesised sizes equal `Measure-Object -Line`, which counts
non-blank lines only; e.g. `tonemapping/mod.rs` is 456 real lines, not 419).

**Row granularity convention.** One row per Bevy entity, in Bevy's declaration order. Where a
group of plain data members shares one status they are enumerated in a single `field` row with each
member's line number (e.g. `CGR-401`); a member gets its own row when its status is independent.
`method` rows carry the verdict where the body cannot diverge from Bevy's shape; a `def` row is
added when the body is the thing that needs checking (pipeline construction, bind-group layouts,
buffer/uniform layouts, specialization keys and shader defs, node ordering, texture allocation,
clear/load/store decisions, LUT handling, dispatch arithmetic).

**Node-label convention (brief, verified).** In the pinned source `#[derive(RenderLabel)]` emits
only `dyn_clone`; label identity is `Interned<dyn RenderLabel>` = (type, value) and there is no
label string. Rows therefore compare the label *type*/variant names, and strings such as
`CopyDeferredLightingIdNode::NAME` are not required counterparts.

**Shader convention.** Epix keeps shaders as embedded Slang string literals inside the
corresponding `.cpp`/`.hpp`. Slang-vs-WGSL is the recorded convention, not a mismatch; the compared
surface is binding indices/stages, entry-point names, arithmetic, and control flow.

**Epix counterparts.** `epix_engine/render/core_graph/**`; `epix_engine/render/render/**` where an
entity lives there (marked `PARENT: render`); `epix_engine/pbr/**` where a `bevy_pbr` consumer of a
core-pipeline entity matters (marked `PARENT: pbr`). `OIT` was absent from Epix and still has one row

Non-✅ rows — the ❌ gaps and 🚫 omissions first, then the recorded ⚠️ divergences:

**Must fix / missing:**

1. *(CGR-520 ✅ fixed in `ac02885e` — the prepass query carries the override, and `run_prepass` applies it.)*
2. *(CGR-526 / CGR-547 ✅ fixed in `ac02885e` — both viewports go through `Viewport::from_viewport_and_override`.)*
3. *(CGR-542 ✅ fixed in `ac02885e` — the deferred query carries the override and both gates.)*
4. **CGR-571 / CGR-580 / CGR-582 ✅** ported in `4997243a`: `OrderIndependentTransparencySettings` (Bevy's two fields and defaults, also the shader's eight-byte uniform), `OIT_REQUIRED_STORAGE_BUFFERS = 2`, and `is_oit_supported` (both device facts as parameters, with Bevy's warning texts). The rest of OIT is still 🚫 — **CGR-572..CGR-579**, **CGR-581**, **CGR-583..CGR-593**: the `Component` impl and its `on_add` warning, `OrderIndependentTransparencyPlugin`, `configure_depth_texture_usages`, `check_msaa`, `OitBuffers`, `init_oit_buffers`, the settings-offset component, `prepare_oit_buffers`, `OitResolvePlugin`, `OitResolveBindGroup`, `OitResolvePipeline`, `OitResolvePipelineId`/`Key`, `queue_`/`specialize_`/`prepare_oit_resolve_*`, `OitResolvePass`, `OitResolveNode`, and both shaders. `PARENT: pbr` already emits `OIT_ENABLED` and an `oit_mesh_pipeline` (`pbr/include/epix/pbr/mesh_pipeline.hpp`, locked by `cluster_tests.cpp:4290-4301`) with no layer buffers to write into, so that shader def is currently inert.
5. **CGR-489 / CGR-490 / CGR-496 / CGR-500** — 🚫 `DepthPrepassDoubleBuffer` and `DeferredPrepassDoubleBuffer` do not exist, and without them `ViewPrepassTextures::{previous_depth_view, previous_deferred_view}` have no source: no Epix view can read the previous frame's depth or deferred G-buffer.
6. **CGR-454** — 🚫 `approximate_inverse_tone_mapping` has no Epix counterpart; its only Bevy consumer is `bevy_pbr` transmission (`pbr_transmission.wgsl:14,78,188`). `PARENT: pbr`.
7. **CGR-446 / CGR-450** — 🚫 `convertNormalizedLog2ToOpenDomain` (dead in Bevy — never called) and `rgb_to_srgb_simple` (bloom re-declares its own copy) are the only two shared shader helpers Epix omits; no core-pipeline behaviour changes.
8. **CGR-637** — ⚠️ `DownsampleDepthNode` has no shadow-map pass: Bevy also downsamples each `OcclusionCullingSubviewEntities` light at `depth_texture_size` (:206-223), so shadow occlusion culling has no pyramid in Epix.
9. **CGR-521 / CGR-545** — ⚠️ `LatePrepassNode` and `LateDeferredGBufferPrepassNode` return immediately instead of running the early body when occlusion culling is on (no early/late bin split yet; C14-D2 / C15-D2). Required alignment: land the bin splitter, then remove both no-ops.

**Recorded intentional divergences (⚠️, rationale in the row):**

10. **CGR-404 / CGR-414 / CGR-456** — no `lut_bindings.wgsl` asset and no `TONEMAPPING_LUT_*_BINDING_INDEX` shader defs: the two LUT bindings are literal `[[vk::binding(3/4)]]` in `tonemapping.slang`. Same indices and stages.
11. **CGR-427 / CGR-428** — the LUTs are decoded by hand into `RGBA32Float` where Bevy keeps the KTX2's native, always-filterable format (REVIEW: on an adapter without 32-bit-float filtering the filterable 3D-texture LUT binding can fail validation; not verifiable read-only), and `lut_placeholder` exists but is never installed because there is no `tonemapping_luts`-off branch.
12. **CGR-410 / CGR-441** — `Tonemapping`'s variant order is rearranged to reproduce Bevy's `#[default]`, and `TONY_MC_MAPFACE_LUT_DIMS` is inlined as literals. Neither has a behavioural effect.
13. **CGR-511** — Epix-only `prepass_pipeline_targets`: the webgpu C++ target array cannot hold a hole, so an unwritten location becomes an `Undefined`-format target (documented, and covered by a skybox test).
14. **CGR-512 / CGR-513 / CGR-514** — `update_previous_view_data`, `prepare_previous_view_uniforms` and `ExtractComponent<PreviousViewData>` are Epix-only in `core_graph`; Bevy's equivalents live in `bevy_pbr`. `PARENT: pbr` must not define a second copy of either system.
15. **CGR-517 / CGR-539 / CGR-544** — `EarlyPrepassNode`'s query drops the optional skybox/previous-view items (looked up in the body instead), the deferred phase items and formats live in `core3d.hpp` rather than a `deferred` module, and `LateDeferredGBufferPrepassNode` is exposed as `Core3dNodes::LateDeferredPrepass` (Bevy's variant name).
16. **CGR-555** — `CopyDeferredLightingIdNode::NAME` has no string counterpart; label identity is the interned (type, value) pair (brief's label note).
17. **CGR-600 / CGR-601 / CGR-612 / CGR-622** — Skybox uniforms are derived in a render-world system instead of inside `ExtractComponent`, and the wasm `SIXTEEN_BYTE_ALIGNMENT` padding is unconditional in the C++ struct (same 80-byte layout).
18. **CGR-617** — `SkyboxPlugin` builds `SkyboxPrepassPipeline` and `PreviousViewUniforms` in one `RenderStartup` closure, because the dynamic buffer needs the device's `minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment`.
19. **CGR-632** — `MipGenerationPlugin` seeds its shader/specialization resources in `attach` and disables itself when the asset registry or server is absent.
20. **CGR-643** — every pyramid storage entry is `ReadWrite` where Bevy marks binding 6 `ReadWrite` and the rest `WriteOnly` (Slang/HLSL have no write-only storage declaration); the access mode is a superset.
21. **CGR-549** — ⛔ Bevy's `webgl && wasm32 && !webgpu` deferred-clear fallback is compiled out natively and has no counterpart; Epix implements the native clear-on-both-nodes behaviour.
22. **CGR-676 / CGR-681** — the `FullscreenMaterial` constraint set is spelled `ShaderWritable` instead of `WriteInto` with component-ness implicit, and `FullscreenMaterialLabel` is a `NodeLabel` subtype instead of a `type_name` wrapper.
23. Structural only, no behavioural consequence: **CGR-459** (`ambiguous_with_all`), **CGR-463** (a no-output-texture guard), **CGR-473** (`allow_ambiguous_resource`), **CGR-652** (max-mips clamped to ≥1 at a zero extent), **CGR-695 / CGR-699** (module surface and plugin list — the only omitted plugin is `OrderIndependentTransparencyPlugin`, which is row 4 above).

# bevy_pbr `render/mesh.rs` — PBR mesh pipeline, keys, instance extraction and bind groups

Block `PBR-100`..`PBR-499`. One row per entity in `bevy_pbr/src/render/mesh.rs`
(3431 lines in the pinned tree, not 3143), plus the `mesh_bindings.rs` /
`mesh_view_bindings.rs` interfaces `mesh.rs` consumes, and — since the block boundary
over the remaining mesh files was lifted — the `prepass/prepass_bindings.rs` and
`light_probe/{environment_map,irradiance_volume}.rs` helpers the view layout adds
(`PBR-281`..`PBR-284`). `mesh.rs` contains **no**
`MeshPipelineViewLayouts`, `MeshPipelineViewLayout`, `MeshPipelinePreprocess` or
`preprocess`: in 0.18 those live in `mesh_view_bindings.rs` and
`gpu_preprocess.rs`, and only the parts `mesh.rs` owns appear here.

**Headline finding:** Epix ports `MeshPipelineKey`, the five blend/depth pass
arms, the shader-def derivation and the morph/skinning layout precedence — and
nothing else. `MeshPipeline`, `MeshRenderPlugin`, every extraction system, every
bind group, `SetMesh*BindGroup` and `DrawMesh` have no counterpart. Epix does have
a *complete* 2D analogue (`epix::sprite_render::Mesh2dPipeline` in
`mesh2d_pipeline.hpp`/`mesh2d_pipeline.cpp`), so the 3D gap is not an absence of
infrastructure — it is an unported pipeline.

## Summary

Counts: ✅ 193 · ❌ 24 · ⚠️ 9 · 🚫 0 · ⛔ 0 · REVIEW 1 (226 rows, `PBR-100`..`PBR-322` plus the `PRT-4`/`PRT-5`/`PRT-6` parent rows).

The 36 ❌ rows are overwhelmingly one fact seen from many angles: **Epix has no 3D mesh pipeline**.
`MeshPipeline`, `MeshRenderPlugin`, the view bind groups and every remaining render command in `mesh.rs`
are absent, and of the extraction stage only the GPU path's query, system and helper are ported —
`MeshExtractionSystems`, the CPU path, the motion-vector flag writer and `collect_meshes_for_gpu_building`
are not. What *is* ported — `MeshPipelineKey` and the view-layout key with every flag, shift and mask
bit-exact (now with Bevy's two compile-time layout assertions), the five pass arms with their blend and
depth-write rules, the shader-def derivation, the morph/skinning layout precedence, and the GPU instance
queues with the two extraction functions that fill them, the eight mesh bind group layouts, the view layout with every entry it names, the pipeline resource that holds it, every mesh shader module it loads but two, and the shared maths library it imports — is ported correctly, plus the three `PARENT: render` rows it found, which is why 187 rows are ✅.

The 9 ⚠️ rows are representation choices (`MainEntity` instead of `RetainedViewEntity`, `glm::mat4` for
`Affine3`, explicit tail padding for `ShaderType` rounding, an unenforced `NonMaxU32` invariant, two maps
plus a tag instead of an enum, one queue instead of `Parallel<…>`), the seven cargo-feature-gated shader
defs (PBR-244), one unwired-but-parity-correct primitive state (PBR-257), one pair of labels with no
descriptor to carry them (PBR-260), and one vertex-layout conversion that exists with its presence
derivation but has no caller yet (PBR-261). The four parameter-only capability fields that used to be
listed here (PBR-189..192) are aligned as of batch 52: `MeshPipeline` owns them.

Non-✅ rows with reasons (rows this batch or an earlier one fixed are kept in place, struck through).

## Not audited

- `mesh_view_bindings.rs` — **the layout half is audited and ported as of batch 50**: the layout keys (PBR-272..276), `MeshPipelineViewLayout` (`PBR-271`), `buffer_layout` (`PBR-297`), `layout_entries` (`PBR-298`), `MeshPipelineViewLayouts` (`PBR-299`) and `generate_view_layouts` (`PBR-300`). What remains is the runtime half — `MeshViewBindGroup` (`PBR-301`) and `prepare_mesh_view_bind_groups` (`PBR-302`) — which needs the device, the pipeline cache and runtime buffers that are not ported.

All of these live in `bevy_pbr/src/render/gpu_preprocess.rs` in 0.18, not in `mesh.rs`; `mesh.rs` only names `PreprocessPipelines`/`PreprocessBindGroups` in `DrawMesh`'s `Param`/`ViewQuery` (PBR-241).

The rest of the block (`mod.rs`'s plugin, extraction/preparation, `generate.rs`, the bindings constructors and the WGSL) is unaudited; `EnvironmentMapUniform`, `MAX_VIEW_LIGHT_PROBES` and `EnvironmentMapUniformBuffer` already existed in `pbr/light_probe.hpp` and are not claimed here.

The rest of the file (`ClusteredDecal` is already ported in `light_cluster.hpp`, but `extract_decals`, `prepare_decals`, `RenderClusteredDecals`, the bind group and the WGSL) is unaudited.

The rest of the block (`ScreenSpaceReflectionsPlugin`, the node, the pipeline and its specialization, the bind group and the WGSL) is unaudited.
- `bevy_pbr/src/atmosphere/**` — only the five shader-data entities the view layout needs are audited and ported (`PBR-292`..`PBR-296`, batch 49): the mode, the two settings forms and their conversion, the GPU atmosphere, and the buffer both go in, because binding 31 is a storage buffer of `AtmosphereData`. Everything that produces or consumes them (`Atmosphere` itself, `ScatteringMedium`, the LUT textures, the environment/render-sky nodes, the plugin and the WGSL) is unaudited.
- `bevy_pbr/src/render/skin.rs` (`SkinUniforms`, `MAX_JOINTS`, `skins_use_uniform_buffers`) and `render/morph.rs` (`MorphUniforms`, `MorphIndices`, `extract_morphs`, `prepare_morphs`) — separate files, separate blocks. Their absence in Epix is visible here only as a consequence (PBR-181, PBR-192, PBR-266), except for `MAX_JOINTS` and `skins_use_uniform_buffers`, which batch 38 ported into `pbr/skin.hpp` because the mesh layouts need them.

Epix keeps all three in `mesh_pipeline_key.hpp:529-588`; parity of values was verified incidentally and they match, but the rows belong to that block.

# `bevy_light` lights, shadows, clusters, probes and fog — PBR light entity audit

Block `PBR-500`..`PBR-899`. One row per entity in `bevy_light/src/{lib,ambient_light,cascade,
directional_light,point_light,spot_light,probe,volumetric}.rs` and `bevy_light/src/cluster/{mod,
assign,test}.rs` in Bevy's own declaration order, plus the light systems that stayed in
`bevy_pbr/src/render/light.rs`, the cluster buffers in `bevy_pbr/src/cluster.rs`, the render-world
visible-entity types in `bevy_pbr/src/components.rs`, and a small set of `PARENT:` rows for the
`render`/`camera`/`transform` entities those files consume.

Three rows in this section may combine mechanically-identical sibling entities (a whole flag-constant
family, a run of scalar fields whose Epix counterpart is one struct with one verdict, a group of
pure accessors). Every named entity of every audited Bevy file still appears in some row; where a
row covers more than one, the Entity cell names all of them.

**Headline finding.** Epix ports the *simulation* half of the 0.18 light split — the component
types, their defaults and constants, the cascade builder and the whole cluster-assignment
arithmetic — and almost none of the *render* half. `LightPlugin`, every render-world extraction and
preparation system (`extract_lights`, `prepare_lights`, `extract_clusters`, `prepare_clusters`,
`init_shadow_samplers`, the three specialisation systems, `queue_shadows`), both shadow-pass graph
nodes and the four render-world visible-entity types are absent, and no plugin registers *anything*
in `epix_engine/pbr` — so the light component types are not even registered as components with
their Bevy required-component relations. Three concrete defects sit inside the code that *is*
ported: cluster assignment never tests `RenderLayers` (assign.rs:541 has no counterpart), it never
writes `Clusters::near`/`far` (assign.rs:455-456), and it neither clears nor resizes
`Clusters::clusterable_objects` (assign.rs:465-477) — so `Clusters` stays empty and the next
`insert_object_into_cluster_row` indexes out of bounds.
