## Summary

| PBR-856 | def | `RenderMaterialInstance`, `RenderMaterialInstances` and the `DUMMY_MESH_MATERIAL` sentinel - the render world's record of which material each mesh uses | `bevy_pbr/src/material.rs:429,571-607` | `epix_engine/pbr/include/epix/pbr/material.hpp` | ✅ | The records are untyped, as Bevy's are, so one map holds every mesh's material whatever type it is. `mesh_material` falls back to the sentinel rather than failing, which is what lets a mesh drawn by a custom pipeline still get a binding, and `current_change_tick` is carried for the sweep. Bevy's sentinel is typed `AssetId<StandardMaterial>` and converted where it is used; `StandardMaterial` is not ported, so it is untyped here and stands for "no material at all". `MaterialRegistry.MeshMaterialFallsBackToTheDummy` checks the fallback. |
| PBR-857 | def | `RenderMaterialBindings` - which bind group slot each prepared material asset was bound at | `bevy_pbr/src/material.rs:1602` | `epix_engine/pbr/include/epix/pbr/material.hpp` | ✅ | The map and a `get` that distinguishes a miss from a binding at slot zero, which is how the GPU instance builder learns a material is not prepared yet and asks for re-extraction instead of drawing with a stale binding. `MaterialRegistry.BindingsDistinguishAMissFromSlotZero` pins that distinction. |
| PBR-858 | def | `MeshMaterial3d<M>(Handle<M>)` - the component that ties a 3D mesh to its material | `bevy_pbr/src/mesh_material.rs:35-41` | `none` | ❌ | Absent, and the prerequisite the 3D material extraction reads: without it a mesh has no way to say which material it uses, so `extract_mesh_materials` (`RenderMaterialInstances`, `PBR-856`) has nothing to read. Its 2D counterpart is ported (`MeshMaterial2d`, `SRD-377`), which is what makes the gap visible. |
| PBR-859 | def | `MeshMaterial3d.0` - the material handle | `bevy_pbr/src/mesh_material.rs:41` | `none` | ❌ | Absent with the type. The 2D counterpart is `SRD-378`. |
| PBR-860 | def | `Default for MeshMaterial3d<M>` - a default handle | `bevy_pbr/src/mesh_material.rs:43-47` | `none` | ❌ | Absent with the type. Bevy's default is `Handle::default()`, and the port's `Handle` deletes its default constructor, so the counterpart is an invalid handle rather than an empty one - the same shape the 2D `Default` took (`SRD-379`, ⚠️ for that reason). |
| PBR-861 | def | `PartialEq`/`Eq for MeshMaterial3d<M>` | `bevy_pbr/src/mesh_material.rs:49-55` | `none` | ❌ | Absent with the type; comparing handles is what change detection reads. The 2D counterpart is `SRD-380`. |

The 5 ❌ rows are the actionable findings, after the eighteen fixed so far
(PBR-707/708/713 in `cf484b87`, PBR-595 in `c43326c0`, PBR-604/605/606/609 in
`9badb75a`, PBR-576/682/798/840 in `636a72c6`, PBR-520/526/530 in
`5d582feb`, PBR-688 in `c698c1fc`, PBR-637 in the light-probe uniform batch and
PBR-826 in `8a08e14a`). One is a diagnostic gap — PBR-796's two
remaining warnings, which need `prepare_lights` — and one is the unread
`NotShadowReceiver` (PBR-508). The other
three are whole-system halves whose pure functions already exist: `prepare_lights`' shadow textures
(PBR-777) and light views (PBR-778), and the `prepare_clusters` system half
(PBR-827), which needs `MeshPipeline` (`PBR-184`) for its binding type.

The 56 🚫 rows are dominated by one fact: **Epix has no render-world light half and no light
plugin.** `LightPlugin`, `ShadowFilteringMethod`, `SimulationLightSystems`, `add_clusters`,
`make_global_cluster_settings`, `init_global_clusterable_object_meta`, `init_shadow_samplers`,
`extract_lights`/`extract_ambient_light*`, `prepare_lights`, `queue_shadows`, `specialize_shadows`,
both shadow graph nodes and the three `Render*VisibleEntities` types are all absent, and nothing in
`epix_engine/pbr` registers a component or a resource. What *is* ported is ported well: the whole
cluster-assignment arithmetic, the cascade split and frustum construction, the GPU uniform layout
(with explicit tail padding where glm's alignment differs from Rust's `ShaderType`), and the
flag/bit contracts all match, which is why 264 rows are ✅.

The 29 ⚠️ rows partition as: enum-payload flattening (5: PBR-653/657/694/771/811), the PCSS
feature-gated light fields (3: PBR-567/585/599), explicit shader-type tail padding where glm's
alignment differs from Rust's `ShaderType` (3: PBR-745/746/750), Windows-macro and `_value`
renamings (3: PBR-663/786/810), `Color`-less linear colours (2: PBR-532/537), typed exceptions in
place of Bevy panics (2: PBR-551/676), the matrix-only `GlobalTransform` decomposition (2:
PBR-561/855), handle defaults (2: PBR-571/613), and one each for the probe-gather type shape
(PBR-635), the build-vs-system split of the directional cascade frusta (PBR-578), raw-set access to
`GlobalVisibleClusterableObjects` (PBR-686), the extra `default_gpu_lights()` factory (PBR-752), the
`PhaseItem` const/non-const overloads (PBR-790) and the `PARENT:` camera helper (PBR-854).

## Not audited

- **Shaders.** `mesh_view_types.wgsl`, `pbr.wgsl`, `shadows.wgsl`, `volumetric_fog.wgsl` and Epix's
  WGSL were not compared. Every flag/bit contract in this section is asserted only on the
  Rust/Epix side; the shader half of "these must match the bit flags in …" is unchecked.
- **Reflection and derive boilerplate.** `Reflect`, `#[reflect(...)]`, `Component`, `Resource`,
  `Deref`/`DerefMut` derives and their Epix equivalents are not rowed beyond the registration rows
  (PBR-502, PBR-687); Epix has no reflection layer to compare against.
- **`bevy_pbr` shader/pipeline internals consumed by `light.rs`.** `PrepassPipeline`,
  `PrepassPipelineSpecializer`, `ErasedMaterialPipelineKey`, `EntitiesNeedingSpecialization`,
  `EntitySpecializationTicks`, `RenderMaterialInstances`, `RenderMeshInstances`,
  `RenderLightmaps`, `ShadowsDrawFunction`, `MeshAllocator::mesh_slabs` and `SlabId` are referenced
  only as the reasons rows PBR-780..PBR-785 are 🚫; none of them was audited against its Epix
  counterpart. `RenderMeshInstances` is covered by the `render/mesh.rs` section.
- **`bevy_pbr/src/render/mesh.rs`.** The `Shadow` phase's plugin registration, `DrawFunctions`,
  `SetMeshBindGroup`/`DrawMesh` and the binned-phase plumbing belong to the `PBR-100`..`PBR-278`
  section (PBR-850 marks the boundary).
- **`bevy_pbr/src/render/light.rs` bodies of the systems recorded as 🚫.** For those rows the
  Bevy body was read and the *capability* it needs is named, but no Epix-side line can exist to
  diff against; the rows are therefore evidence of absence, not line-level comparison.
- **`bevy_pbr/src/light_probe/mod.rs` beyond the gather defs.** Only lines 300-419 and 550-651
  were read, for PBR-627..PBR-640; the rest of that file (bind groups, texture binding arrays,
  `upload_light_probes`' body) was not audited.
- **Epix tests.** `epix_engine/pbr/tests/header/cluster_tests.cpp` (4927 lines) was
  grep-scanned, not read in full. It is cited only as evidence that a behaviour is exercised — in
  particular `assign_objects_to_clusters` at `:3508` pre-resizes `clusterable_objects`, which is
  what proves PBR-708's missing resize is real rather than a call-order artefact.
- **The `DistanceFog` half of `epix_engine/pbr/src/fog.cpp`.** `prepare_fog` is Bevy's
  distance-fog system (`bevy_pbr/src/fog.rs`), a different module from
  `bevy_light/src/volumetric.rs`; PBR-650 records the boundary.
- **`epix_engine/pbr/tests/**` and `epix_engine/pbr/include/epix/pbr/{mesh_pipeline,
  mesh_pipeline_key,mesh_instance,mesh_uniform,material_bindings}.hpp`** — out of this section's
  scope; they belong to `PBR-100`..`PBR-278`.

## Not yet audited

The six modules are only partly covered: the sections above audit specific Bevy files. Still open, so the next round knows where to start —

- **`mesh` (`MSH-`, `PRT-`)** — the `mesh.rs` support files with no section yet: `bevy_mesh/src/vertex.rs` (`VertexAttributeValues` internals, `VertexBufferLayout`, `MeshVertexBufferLayout`, `MeshVertexBufferLayouts`, `MissingVertexAttributeError` bodies), `index.rs`, `components.rs`, `skinning.rs`, `morph.rs`, `lib.rs` (the `MeshPlugin` entity), `conversions.rs`, `mikktspace.rs` — against `epix_engine/mesh/include/epix/mesh/{vertex_attribute_values.hpp,vertex_buffer_layout.hpp,components.hpp}`. The mesh primitive builders are also unaudited: `bevy_mesh/src/primitives/**` against `epix_engine/mesh/include/epix/mesh/primitives.hpp` and `epix_engine/mesh/src/primitives.cpp` (`Triangle3d::mesh()`, `Triangle3dMeshBuilder`, `Measured2d`/`Measured3d`, `Inset`), plus the `bevy_math` primitive shapes they mirror (`bevy_math/src/primitives/**`; `Aabb3d` lives in `bevy_math::bounding`, and `Triangle3d` — whose MSH-218 row is already open — has its home there too). `mesh/src/mesh_factory.cpp` is Epix-only and has no Bevy file to diff.
- **`image` (`IMG-`)** — `image.rs` and the loader/conversion/atlas/decoder files are covered (`image-image_rs.md`, `image-loader-atlas.md`); still open: the `PARENT: render` consumers (`GpuImage`/`RenderAsset<Image>` preparation, `fallback_image.hpp`, `screenshot.cpp`). `bevy_image/src/ktx2.rs` and `dds.rs` are enumerated at declaration level only (Epix has no counterpart for either file), and the unused surface of the pinned `rectangle-pack`/`guillotiere` crates is out of scope by design.
- **`pbr` (`PBR-`)** — beyond `render/mesh.rs` and the light set now covered by `pbr-lights.md`: `material.rs`, `material_bind_groups.rs`, the `mesh_bindings.rs` per-entry layout builders and the whole of `mesh_view_bindings.rs` (`MeshPipelineViewLayouts`, `MeshPipelineViewLayout`, `generate_view_layouts`, `layout_entries`, `MeshViewBindGroup`), `render/skin.rs`, `render/morph.rs`, `render/gpu_preprocess.rs` (`MeshPipelinePreprocess`, `preprocess`, `PreprocessPipelines`, `PreprocessBindGroups`, `IndirectParametersBuffers`), `lightmap/mod.rs`, `meshlet/**`, `deferred/**`, `ssr/**` and `volumetric_fog/**` against `epix_engine/pbr/**`.
- **`render/core_graph` (`CGR-`)** — the Bevy files both CGR blocks reference but do not own: `bevy_core_pipeline/src/prepass/node.rs` internals, `deferred/copy_lighting_id.rs` (CGR-200 is ⛔ for exactly that reason), `msaa_writeback.rs`, `bevy_render/src/view/mod.rs`, `bevy_camera/**`; and the Epix files outside the audited set (`core_graph/src/prepass.cpp`, `mip_generation.cpp`, `skybox.cpp`, `tonemapping.cpp`, `upscaling.cpp`, `blit.cpp`, `plugin.cpp` internals), which the rows cite only where they register or consume an audited label.
- **Bevy subsystems with no Epix counterpart at all** — each is visible today only as ⛔/🚫 rows and needs a scope decision (port it, or record it as ⛔ with a rationale) before the module can be called aligned: atmosphere, decal/clustered decals, deferred materials, lightmap, meshlet, SSAO, SSR, volumetric fog, wireframe, picking (`bevy_picking`; all of SPR-424..SPR-435), order-independent transparency (CGR-571..CGR-593), render diagnostics (`pass_span`/`diagnostic_recorder`; CGR-208/218/226/294/301), the `bevy_solari` raytracing path, and asset reflection.

## Maintenance rules

- **A row's ID is stable.** `MSH-`/`IMG-`/`SPR-`/`SRD-`/`PBR-`/`CGR-`/`PRT-` IDs are never reused, renumbered or deleted, and rows are never merged into one or dropped; an ID block, once allocated to a Bevy file, keeps its numbering, so a commit message, an approval request and a later re-audit all refer to the same mismatch.
- **A fixed row moves to ✅ with the fixing commit**, carrying the evidence the row needs: the focused module tests for logic-only/value-only changes, or a whole-tree build plus the full CTest sweep plus the example sweep on both output streams plus stable client-area captures for anything that can affect rendering (see `_policy.md`, "Verification policy").
- **The Audit index counts are recomputed, never hand-edited.** Adding or merging a section means re-parsing the row tables under `tmp/audit/sections/**` and recomputing every count; where a section's prose summary disagrees with its own rows, the computed number wins and the disagreement is recorded as a footnote under the index (see the `mesh-lead-verified.md` footnote).
- **A section file may only be merged into this file verbatim.** The files under `tmp/audit/sections/` are the working papers — they may be edited, split or superseded — while this file is the record: `## Audited sections` reproduces each one under its `<!-- section: … -->` marker without rewriting, renumbering, reordering or summarising a single row, and a correction is made in the section file and re-merged rather than patched here.
- **Every non-✅ row appears in the Open mismatch index, and every non-✅ `PARENT:`/`PRT-` row in the parent-module table** — a `PARENT:` marker counts wherever the section puts it, in the difference cell or in the Entity/Epix cell, so a divergence recorded only on the entity is not missed; the ✅ rows a section marked `PARENT:` in the difference cell stay in the table as coverage evidence. A new section must extend both tables; a row that reaches ✅ leaves the Open mismatch index and stays in the merged section as coverage evidence.
- **A parent-module fix is approved before committing** (`render`, `app`, `ecs`, `assets`, `camera`, `transform`, …): the mismatch IDs, the changed files and the evidence go to the user first, and a parent module that turns out to diverge is audited again rather than patched around.
- **A new section file is merged verbatim; only the counts and the two index tables are recomputed.** Adding a section appends its file under `## Audited sections` behind a `<!-- section: … -->` marker in the declared order, then re-derives the Audit index counts, the Open mismatch index and the parent-module table from the parsed rows; the hand-written prose, the fix batches and the already-merged sections are copied unchanged.
